mainTopic: Mistaken substitution (שוגג in תמורה), animals that cannot become holy or make a תמורה, and whether a consecrated טריפה gets קדושת הגוף.
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's list of ways תמורה differs from regular הקדש. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a mistaken (שוגג) substitution still counts, and the גמרא finds the source in the words "יהיה קדש". Then several אמוראים (חזקיה, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן, and רב ששת) each describe a different kind of mistake that the rule covers. Next, שמואל explains רבי אלעזר's rule that כלאים, טריפה, יוצא דופן, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס neither become holy nor make a תמורה. רבי מאיר shows when such animals could ever be holy in the first place. רב פפא and רבא try several times to explain why these animals are like a בהמה טמאה and not like a בעל מום. Finally, שמואל rules that a consecrated טריפה stays holy until it dies, while רבי אושעיא says it is only like consecrated wood and stones. The גמרא then challenges שמואל from a משנה and from רבי מאיר's ברייתא.

steps.title: End of the משנה's clause: the substitute is never released for shearing and work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its point that a תמורה with a permanent blemish never goes out to become חולין, so it can never be sheared or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The substitute does not go out to become non-sacred so that it can) be sheared and be worked.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a sentence in the משנה that started on the previous page. They finish the משנה's point about a substitute animal that has a permanent blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is listing ways that תמורה is stricter than regular הקדש. A blemished animal that was made holy directly can be redeemed, and then people may shear it and work with it. A תמורה, however, never loses its holiness that way, so shearing and working with it stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To be sheared (have its wool cut)
To be worked (used for labor, like plowing)

steps.confusionAlert: These two words are not a new teaching. They are the end of a sentence that began before this section, about a תמורה that never goes out to חולין.

phrases.english: to be sheared and to be worked.
phrases.notes: This finishes the משנה's sentence: a blemished substitute never becomes ordinary, so you can't shear it or use it for work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's comparison of תמורה and הקדש, which continues here from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה with a permanent blemish never goes out to חולין, so shearing it and working with it are never allowed.

steps.title: Mistaken substitution counts, but mistaken consecration does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds one more difference: by תמורה, a שוגג is treated like a מזיד, but by ordinary מוקדשין it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: The Torah treated one who acts by mistake like one who acts on purpose when it comes to substitution. It did not treat one who acts by mistake like one who acts on purpose when it comes to consecrated items.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives another way that תמורה is stricter than regular הקדש. A substitution done by mistake still takes effect, but a consecration done by mistake does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a holy status only comes when a person means it. By תמורה, even a person who acted by mistake makes the second animal holy. By ordinary הקדש, a mistaken consecration has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who acts by mistake, without realizing
Someone who acts on purpose, knowingly
Substitution: trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one. Both animals become holy.
Things that were made holy (consecrated) directly

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section explains where this rule comes from and what kind of "mistake" it means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
It made one acting by mistake like one acting on purpose with substitution,
but it did not make one acting by mistake like one acting on purpose with consecrated items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another difference to the משנה's list of ways תמורה is stricter than הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistaken תמורה takes effect like an intentional one. A mistaken consecration does not take effect.

steps.title: Five kinds of animals that cannot become holy or make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר lists five kinds of animals that do not become holy and cannot make another animal holy through תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: An animal that is a mix of two species, a טרפה, one born by caesarean section, a טומטום, and an אנדרוגינוס do not become holy, and they do not make other animals holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר names five types of animals that cannot be offered. He rules that they cannot become holy as קרבנות, and they cannot make a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא קדושין" means consecrating one of these animals does not give it the holiness of a קרבן. "ולא מקדישין" means that even if the animal was holy before (for example, it became a טרפה later), it cannot pass holiness to a regular animal through תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species
An animal with a fatal defect
An animal born by caesarean section, through the side
An animal whose gender cannot be seen
An animal with both male and female organs
They do not become holy, and they do not make others holy

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two rules. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a שוגג counts by תמורה but not by הקדש. רבי אלעזר says five unfit kinds of animals neither become holy nor make a תמורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
An animal of mixed species, and a tereifa, and one born by caesarean section,
and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite —
are not holy, and do not make holy.
phrases.notes: "Do not make holy" means they can't pass holiness to another animal by swapping it, which is תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement in the משנה about which animals can become holy or make a תמורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלאים, טרפה, יוצא דופן, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס do not become holy and do not make a תמורה.

steps.title: What is the source for counting a mistaken substitution?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the reason behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule that a שוגג counts like a מזיד by תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts and asks where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gets his rule from. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person who acts by mistake is not treated like one who acts on purpose. So the גמרא wants a source that shows תמורה is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is the reason? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי טעמא דרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in step 2 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source shows that a mistaken תמורה takes effect?

steps.title: The extra words "יהיה קדש" include a mistaken substitution
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק: the words "יהיה קדש" come to include a שוגג like a מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "it shall be holy". This comes to include one who acts by mistake like one who acts on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is in the פסוק about תמורה. The word "יהיה" teaches that even a mistaken substitution makes the animal holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said the animal is holy. The extra word "יהיה" ("shall be") is read as a לרבות, adding another case: the animal becomes holy even when the person acted by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall be holy"
To include (an extra case)

phrases.english: The verse states: "shall be holy,"
to include one acting by mistake like one acting on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words "יהיה קדש" in the פסוק of תמורה include a שוגג like a מזיד.

steps.title: What kind of mistake is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case of שוגג the rule is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of one acting by mistake who is treated like one acting on purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of mistaken substitution counts. This question sets up חזקיה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "By mistake" could mean many things. For example, the person might not have meant to say the words at all, or he might not have known the law. The גמרא wants the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of one acting by mistake like one acting on purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the source is known, the גמרא asks what case it covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly counts as a שוגג for this rule?

steps.title: חזקיה: he thought substituting was allowed
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה explains the case. The person thought it was allowed to substitute. By תמורה he gets מלקות, but in the matching case by קדשים he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: It is when he thought it was permitted to substitute. With substitution he gets lashes. With consecrated animals he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה says the "mistake" means the person knew what he was doing but thought substituting was allowed. In that case, by תמורה he is still punished with מלקות, but in the matching case by הקדש he is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person meant to do the act and only didn't know it was forbidden. The extra "יהיה" makes him like a מזיד by תמורה, so the swap takes effect and he gets מלקות. By ordinary קדשים, for example wrongly consecrating an unfit animal, this kind of mistake does not bring מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: To substitute (to do a תמורה)
He receives lashes (מלקות)
With regard to, in the case of
Animals made holy directly (ordinary consecration)

steps.whatToRemember: By תמורה, even a person who thought substituting was allowed is treated as if he did it on purpose. He gets מלקות because of "יהיה קדש". By ordinary קדשים, the same kind of mistake does not bring מלקות.
steps.confusionAlert: The mistake here is not about the action. He knew he was swapping animals. He just thought swapping was allowed.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
As when one thinks that it is permitted to substitute.
With regard to substitution — he is lashed,
with regard to consecrated animals — he is not lashed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר חזקיה כסבור שהוא מותר להמיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by describing the exact case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שוגג is someone who thought substituting was allowed. By תמורה he gets מלקות, but by קדשים he does not.

steps.title: Another version of חזקיה: the substitute becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, חזקיה's point is about whether the animal becomes holy, not about מלקות. By תמורה it becomes holy, and by קדשים it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: by תמורה, the animal becomes holy. By קדשים, it does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way of reporting חזקיה's answer from step 7. Here the difference between תמורה and קדשים is about whether the animal becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the difference was about מלקות: he gets lashes by תמורה but not by קדשים. In this version the difference is about the animal itself. A mistaken תמורה still makes the animal holy, but a mistaken הקדש does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a different way the same teaching was reported
It becomes holy
Animals made holy directly (הקדש), not by תמורה

phrases.english: Another version:
By a substitute, it becomes holy;
by holy offerings, it does not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of חזקיה's answer from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of שוגג is meant by the rule that a שוגג counts like a מזיד by תמורה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistaken person's substitute becomes holy by תמורה, but in the matching case by קדשים the animal does not become holy.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן: meant to say עולה but said שלמים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן give a different case of שוגג. The person meant to make the animal a substitute for his עולה but said it was a substitute for his שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן say: the case is where he meant to say 'a substitute for an עולה' and he said 'a substitute for a שלמים'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים answer the question from step 6 with a different case. The mistake here is a slip of the tongue about which offering he was switching for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חזקיה, the mistake was thinking that substituting is allowed. Here the person knows the law, but he says the wrong offering's name. Even so, the תמורה still takes effect, while a matching slip by הקדש would not.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who meant to say: he intended one word and said another
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
A peace offering, mostly eaten by the owners

phrases.english: Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan say:
It is like one who meant to say "a substitute for a burnt offering,"
and he said "a substitute for a peace offering."
phrases.notes: The rest is understood from before: by תמורה he gets lashes, and in the matching case by קדשים he does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי: כְּסָבוּר לוֹמַר ״תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different case from חזקיה's, answering the same question from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of שוגג is meant?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slip of the tongue: he meant to say 'substitute for an עולה' but said 'substitute for a שלמים'.

steps.title: Another version of ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן: the substitute becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: In this version of the עולה/שלמים case, the point is that the substitute of the שלמים becomes holy, but a matching mistake by קדשים does not make the animal holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: by a substitute for a שלמים, it becomes holy. By קדשים, it does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like in step 8, the גמרא brings a second version. This time it is a second version of the case of ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case stays the same: a slip between עולה and שלמים. The only change is what the difference is about. It is no longer about מלקות. It is about whether the animal actually becomes holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, in the case of
An animal given as a substitute for a שלמים
It does not become holy

phrases.english: Another version:
By a substitute for a peace offering, it becomes holy;
by holy offerings, it does not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרַת שְׁלָמִים — קָדֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer of ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the difference between תמורה and קדשים in the עולה/שלמים slip?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The substitute of the שלמים becomes holy, but a matching slip by קדשים does not make the animal holy.

steps.title: Another version: meant to say black but said white
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the slip is about which animal he named: he meant to say 'black' but said 'white'. By תמורה he gets lashes, but by קדשים he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: like one who meant to say 'black' and said 'white'. By תמורה he gets lashes; by קדשים he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more version of the slip-of-the-tongue case. This time the mistake is about which animal he meant, not which offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistake now is in naming the animal that becomes the substitute: the white one instead of the black one. By תמורה, the white animal still counts, so he gets מלקות. By קדשים, the same slip does not make the animal holy, so there are no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Black
White
He gets lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: Another version:
It is like one who meant to say "black"
phrases.notes: He means the animal: he wanted to name the black animal, but he named the white one.

phrases.english: and he said "white":
by a substitute, he gets lashes;
by holy offerings, he does not get lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the עולה/שלמים slip with a different slip: black versus white.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of שוגג is meant?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He meant to say black but said white. By תמורה he gets lashes, by קדשים he does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'Let this one go out and that one come in'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives another case. A person says 'let this one go out and this one come in', thinking he can move the holiness off one animal and onto another. By תמורה he gets lashes. The matching case by קדשים is someone who thinks blemished קדשים may be eaten without פדיון, and he does not get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the case is one who says 'let this one go out and let this one come in.' By קדשים, the matching case is one who says that animals that got a blemish may be eaten without redemption: he does not get lashes. By תמורה, he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question of step 6 with a new kind of mistake. The person is wrong about how holiness works, not just slipping with his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person thinks that saying 'let this one go out' really takes the holiness off the first animal. It does not, but the new animal still becomes a תמורה, so he gets מלקות. The matching mistake by קדשים is thinking a blemished animal may be eaten without פדיון. There the mistake does count as an excuse, and he does not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let this one go out and let this one come in: trying to move holiness from one animal to another
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
Redemption: paying to move the holiness onto money
They may be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא gives a different case of a mistaken person. In every case, the mistake does not stop תמורה from taking effect, but a matching mistake by קדשים does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that תמורה is stricter than הקדש: it takes effect, and brings מלקות, even when the person acted by mistake.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
It is when one says, "Let this one go out, and let this one come in."
phrases.notes: He thinks the holiness leaves the first animal and moves onto the second one.

phrases.english: By holy offerings, it is when one says
that ones that got a blemish
may be eaten without redemption:
he does not get lashes;
by a substitute, he gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּאוֹמֵר ״תֵּצֵא זוֹ וְתִיכָּנֵס זוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one more answer to the question of step 6, with a mistake about the law instead of a slip of the tongue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of שוגג is meant?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who says 'let this one go out and this one come in' gets lashes by תמורה. The matching case by קדשים, eating a blemished animal without פדיון by mistake, brings no lashes.

steps.title: רב ששת: planning on purpose, acting absentmindedly
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives another case of a שוגג in תמורה. A person declares ahead of time that he will consecrate and substitute knowingly, but when the time comes he acts without paying attention. For תמורה he gets lashes, but for קדשים he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is a case where one says, 'I will enter this house and consecrate, and I will substitute knowingly.' Then he went in and substituted and consecrated without paying attention. For the תמורה he gets lashes. For the קדשים he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds one more example of how someone could make a תמורה by mistake and still get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another answer to the same question as steps 9-12: what kind of שוגג gets lashes for תמורה? Here the person made his plan on purpose, but the act itself happened absentmindedly. That is enough for lashes by תמורה, but the matching case by קדשים brings no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowingly; with my full intent
Without his attention; absentmindedly
He gets lashes (מלקות)

steps.whatToRemember: All the cases from חזקיה, ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן and רב ששת answer the same question from step 6. Some kind of mistaken תמורה still takes effect and brings lashes, while the matching mistake by קדשים does not.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is a case where one says: "I will enter this house
and consecrate," and "I will substitute, knowingly,"
and he went in and substituted and consecrated without paying attention —
regarding תמורה, he gets lashes;
regarding consecrated animals, he does not get lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer alongside רבי יוחנן's cases, defining the שוגג who gets lashes for תמורה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שוגג case is one where he declared his intent in advance but acted absentmindedly. He gets lashes for תמורה but not for קדשים.

steps.title: שמואל explains רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר in the משנה about כלאים, טריפה and similar animals. שמואל explains that the rule has two parts. These animals do not become holy as a תמורה, and if they are holy, they cannot make another animal holy as their תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: The crossbred animal and the טריפה, etc. שמואל said: They do not become holy through תמורה, and they do not make another animal holy by making a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new part of the משנה, רבי אלעזר's rule, and שמואל explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate directions here. First, if you try to make one of these animals the substitute, it does not become holy. Second, if one of these animals is the holy one, swapping a regular animal for it does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species
An animal with a fatal defect
They become holy
They make something else holy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two halves. 'לא קדושין' is about the animal itself getting holiness. 'לא מקדישין' is about it passing holiness to a different animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
The crossbred animal and the טריפה, etc.
Shmuel said:
They do not become holy through תמורה,
and they do not make holy, to create a תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי אלעזר's clause in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These animals cannot become a holy תמורה, and if they are holy they cannot create a תמורה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר asks how such animals could make anything holy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's question. If these animals cannot become holy, how could we even talk about them making another animal holy?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא. רבי מאיר said: But since they don't become holy, how could they make another animal holy?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר points out a problem with the second half of the rule. This sets up his answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make a תמורה, the original animal must already be holy. But these animals can't become holy in the first place. So it seems pointless to say they 'cannot make a תמורה', because when would they ever be holy?

keyTerms.meaning: Since; given that
From where; how could it be

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Meir said:
But since they do not become holy,
how could they make another holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second half of the rule שמואל explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause 'ולא מקדישין' in רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal that can never be holy can never be in a position to make a תמורה, so the clause seems to have nothing to apply to.

steps.title: Holiness that came first: טריפה and יוצא דופן
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that the rule applies when the holiness came first. Someone consecrated a healthy animal and it later became a טריפה. Or someone consecrated an unborn calf and it was then born through the side (יוצא דופן).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you only find it when someone consecrates an animal and afterward it became a טריפה, or when someone consecrates an unborn calf and it came out through the side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר begins his answer by showing real cases where these animals are already holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal became holy while it was still fine. The problem (טריפה, or a birth through the side) came only afterward. Now it is a holy animal, and the rule teaches that it still cannot make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a טריפה
An unborn calf / offspring
Was born through the side, by a cut (like a C-section)

phrases.english: Rather, you only find it
when one consecrates an animal and afterward it became a טריפה,
or when one consecrates an unborn calf and it came out [by way of] the side.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּמַקְדִּישׁ בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's own question for טריפה and יוצא דופן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: the holiness came before the defect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These animals could never be holy, so 'לא מקדישין' has no case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They can be holy if the holiness came first. Even then, they cannot make a תמורה.

steps.title: כלאים, טומטום, אנדרוגינוס: only as holy offspring
steps.stepSummary: For כלאים, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, a case only exists with the offspring of holy animals (ולדי קדשים). That works according to רבי יהודה, who holds that such offspring can make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But crossbred animals, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, you only find with the offspring of holy animals. And that is according to רבי יהודה, who said the offspring makes a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר finishes his answer for the other animals on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals are this way from birth, so you can't consecrate them first and have the problem come later. They can only be holy by being born to a holy mother. And the rule matters only if offspring can make a תמורה at all, which is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose gender cannot be seen
An animal with signs of both genders
Offspring of consecrated animals, holy from birth
According to the view of

phrases.english: But crossbred animals, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּוַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: you only find it with the offspring of holy animals,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: the offspring makes a תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's answer for the animals that are this way from birth.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation tied to one תנא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: For these animals, the rule applies only to holy offspring, and only according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב פפא asks for רבי אלעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks why רבי אלעזר holds that these animals cannot be holy and cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What is רבי אלעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's rule. He answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא explained what the rule says and when it applies. Now it asks why these animals should be treated this way at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the rule to explaining its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind רבי אלעזר's rule.

steps.title: Like a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא compares these animals to a בהמה טמאה. A non-kosher animal is never offered, and קדושת הגוף does not rest on it. In the same way, these animals are not offered and קדושת הגוף does not rest on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are like a non-kosher animal. Just as a non-kosher animal is not offered and holiness of the body does not come onto it, so too these are not offered and holiness of the body does not come onto them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers his own question with a comparison to a non-kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real body-holiness (קדושת הגוף) only comes onto an animal that can be brought on the מזבח. These animals can never be offered, so they are treated like a בהמה טמאה. That is why they do not become holy as a תמורה and do not pass holiness on.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal
Is offered as a קרבן
Holiness on the animal's body itself, not just on its value
Comes down onto; takes hold

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's rule rests on a comparison to a בהמה טמאה. Steps 20-26 test exactly what that comparison is based on.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties תמורה to קדושת הגוף. Only an animal fit for the מזבח can take part in substitution.

phrases.english: Like a non-kosher animal —
just as a non-kosher animal is not offered
and holiness of the body does not come onto it,
so too these are not offered
and holiness of the body does not come onto them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These animals are like a בהמה טמאה: they cannot be offered, so קדושת הגוף never takes hold of them.

steps.title: Why not compare them to a blemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: a בעל מום is also never offered, yet קדושת הגוף rests on it. So why compare these animals to a בהמה טמאה instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But look at a blemished animal. It is not offered, and still bodily holiness rests on it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the comparison to a בהמה טמאה. He points to a בעל מום, which is also not offered but still becomes holy in its body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 19 was: not offered, so no קדושת הגוף. A בעל מום breaks that pattern, because it is not offered yet it does get קדושת הגוף. So 'not offered' alone cannot be the reason, and maybe these animals should be treated like a בעל מום.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a physical blemish that disqualifies it from the altar
Holiness of the body itself, as opposed to holiness of its money value only
But look at…, a word that brings a counter-example

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But there is a blemished animal, which is not offered,
and yet bodily holiness comes upon it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison to a בהמה טמאה from step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning 'not offered, so no קדושת הגוף'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בעל מום is not offered, yet it has קדושת הגוף, so not being offered does not stop holiness from resting on the body.

steps.title: A blemished animal's kind is offered
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a בעל מום is different, because animals of its kind (unblemished ones) are offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A blemished animal is offered in its kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the בעל מום does not fit the comparison. Its type of animal, healthy cows and sheep, does go on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is no longer 'is this animal offered?' but 'is its kind ever offered?' A blemished sheep belongs to a kind that is offered. A בהמה טמאה has no kind that is ever offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Its kind is offered: other animals of the same type do go on the altar

phrases.english: He said to him:
A blemished animal is offered in its kind.
phrases.notes: He means healthy animals of the same type are offered, even if this blemished one is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the animal itself vs. its kind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בעל מום is not offered, so it should be just like a בהמה טמאה
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום's kind is offered, so it is not like a בהמה טמאה

steps.title: But a טריפה's kind is also offered
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects: by that logic, a טריפה's kind is also offered, so it should get קדושת הגוף too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a טריפה too: its kind is offered!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא turns רבא's answer against him. A טריפה also comes from a kind of animal that goes on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'its kind is offered' is enough for holiness, then a טריפה should become holy just like a בעל מום. But רבי אלעזר says a טריפה does not become holy, so this answer does not work for רבי אלעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect or injury
If so, a phrase that turns an answer into a problem

phrases.english: If so,
a טריפה also is offered in its kind!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, טְרֵפָה נָמֵי קָא קָרְבָה בְּמִינָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's test of 'its kind is offered'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טריפה also passes this test, so it should become holy, which goes against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Defect in the body vs. something missing
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. A בהמה טמאה has a defect of its basic nature (פסול הגוף), and so do these animals. A בעל מום only has a defect of something missing (פסול חסרון).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Like a non-kosher animal. Just as a non-kosher animal is disqualified in its body, so too anything disqualified in its body. This excludes a blemished animal, which is disqualified because something is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops his first answer and finds a new way to tell the two groups apart. The question is what kind of defect the animal has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the comparison to a בהמה טמאה is about the type of defect. A טריפה, טומטום and the others have a defect in their very nature, like a בהמה טמאה. A בעל מום is only lacking a limb, so it can still become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A defect in the animal's basic nature or body
A defect of something missing, like a lacking limb
To exclude, showing what the rule leaves out
Rather, which drops the earlier answer for a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: Like a non-kosher animal,
just as a non-kosher animal is disqualified in its body,
so too anything disqualified in its body,
to exclude a blemished animal,
which is a disqualification of something missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops step 21's answer because of step 22 and offers a new distinction
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction based on the type of defect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is whether the animal's kind is offered
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is a defect of the body itself vs. a defect of something missing

steps.title: Some blemishes are also defects of the body
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא challenges רבא: the Torah's passage on blemishes includes שרוע and קלוט, and those are defects of the body, not something missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said to רבא: But isn't 'too long' and 'closed' written in the passage, and these are defects of the body!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא points to two blemishes in the Torah's list. They are not about anything missing, so רבא's new rule does not fit them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said every בעל מום is a case of something missing. But שרוע, a limb too long, and קלוט, closed hooves, are extra or changed body parts, which are defects of the body. Since they are still counted as blemishes, the line between בעל מום and פסול הגוף falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with one limb longer than the matching limb
An animal with closed, uncloven hooves
In the Torah passage, here the passage listing blemishes

phrases.english: Rav Adda said to Rava:
But isn't 'too long' and 'closed' written in the passage,
and these are disqualifications of the body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction given in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a בעל מום is only a פסול חסרון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah lists שרוע and קלוט as blemishes, yet they are defects of the body, so not every blemish is a case of something missing.

steps.title: Nothing of its kind is ever offered
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a final explanation. A בהמה טמאה has no kind that is ever offered, and so too these animals, while a בעל מום does have a kind that is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Like a non-kosher animal. Just as a non-kosher animal has none of its kind offered, so too anything that has none of its kind offered. This excludes a blemished animal, because its kind is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the 'type of defect' answer and explains the comparison to a בהמה טמאה in a new way. The question is whether there is any of its kind that goes on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בהמה טמאה is cut off from the altar as a whole category. The animals רבי אלעזר discusses are treated the same way, while a בעל מום comes from a kind that is offered. This is the same idea as רבא's first answer in step 21, now stated as the full comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: There is none of its kind, meaning none of its type is offered
There is some of its kind, meaning its type is offered

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר, these animals are like a בהמה טמאה, because nothing of their kind goes on the altar. A בעל מום is different because animals of its kind are offered.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three answers. Step 21's idea ('its kind is offered') was dropped because of טריפה. Step 23 ('defect of the body') was dropped because of שרוע and קלוט. Step 25 brings back the 'its kind' idea as the full comparison.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: Like a non-kosher animal,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: just as a non-kosher animal has none of its kind offered,
so too anything that has none of its kind offered,
to exclude a blemished animal,
since there is some of its kind offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, מָה בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה דְּלֵיכָּא בְּמִינַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops step 23's distinction because of step 24 and goes back to the 'its kind' idea
steps.terutzResolutionType: Returning to an earlier distinction as the final explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is a defect of the body vs. a defect of something missing
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is whether any of the animal's kind is offered on the altar

steps.title: A טריפה is like a non-kosher animal because both are forbidden to eat
steps.stepSummary: The earlier challenge was that a טריפה also has animals of its kind that are offered. The answer: a טריפה is not like a בעל מום, because a טריפה, like a בהמה טמאה, is forbidden to eat, while a בעל מום may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you say, that a טריפה has its kind offered? It is still not like a בעל מום. A בהמה טמאה is forbidden to eat, and a טריפה is forbidden to eat. That leaves out a בעל מום, which may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב פפא's challenge about a טריפה and answers it. A טריפה belongs with the בהמה טמאה group because neither one may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that 'its kind is offered' should give a טריפה קדושת הגוף, just like a בעל מום. The answer brings in a new point that splits them: a טריפה and a בהמה טמאה are both forbidden as food, while a בעל מום is allowed. So the טריפה stays in the group that does not get קדושת הגוף.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it is forbidden to eat
Of its kind, meaning healthy animals of the same type that are brought as offerings
Forbidden to eat
To exclude; this leaves out a different case

steps.whatToRemember: A טריפה is grouped with a בהמה טמאה, not with a בעל מום. The reason is that both are forbidden to eat, while a בעל מום is permitted.

phrases.english: What did you say?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב פפא's challenge from earlier.

phrases.english: That a tereifa has its kind offered?
It is not similar to a blemished animal,
a non-kosher animal is forbidden to eat,
and a tereifa is forbidden to eat,
which excludes a blemished animal
that is permitted to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the טריפה challenge from step 22, which still stood against רבא's final answer in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further difference: whether the animal may be eaten.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a טריפה's kind is offered, it should be like a בעל מום and get קדושת הגוף.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טריפה is forbidden to eat, like a בהמה טמאה, so it does not get קדושת הגוף. A בעל מום may be eaten, so it is different.

steps.title: שמואל: a consecrated טריפה needs a permanent blemish to be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if someone consecrates a טריפה, it can only be redeemed once it has a מום קבוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: if someone consecrates a טריפה, it needs a permanent blemish before it can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. שמואל gives a ruling about what happens when someone consecrates an animal that is already a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, needing a מום קבוע before פדיון is the rule for an animal with קדושת הגוף. So שמואל seems to treat a consecrated טריפה as having real body-sanctity, even though it can never be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates something
A permanent blemish
To redeem, meaning to remove the sanctity by paying its value

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who consecrates a tereifa,
it requires a permanent blemish
in order to redeem it because of that blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about consecrating a טריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A consecrated טריפה cannot be redeemed until it has a מום קבוע.

steps.title: Would that mean redeeming sacred animals to feed to dogs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. If a טריפה can be redeemed, its meat can only go to dogs, and we do not redeem consecrated animals for dog food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we learn from this that one may redeem consecrated animals to feed them to dogs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling. Redeeming a טריפה would only be useful for feeding it to dogs, and that is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה's meat is forbidden to people, so after פדיון it would only be dog food. There is a known rule that we do not redeem קדשים just to feed them to dogs. So שמואל's ruling, which allows פדיון after a מום, seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; here it is asked as a challenging question
Consecrated animals
To feed them to dogs

phrases.english: Shall we learn from this
that one redeems consecrated animals
in order to feed them to dogs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a consecrated טריפה can be redeemed once it has a מום קבוע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeeming a טריפה would only be for dog food, and that goes against the accepted rule.

steps.title: שמואל rephrased: the sanctity lasts until the animal dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of שמואל's statement. A consecrated טריפה becomes holy 'to die'. It is never redeemed and simply stays holy until it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: it creates sanctity to die. In other words, the טריפה stays holy until its death and cannot be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes שמואל's statement so it no longer has the dog-food problem. The טריפה becomes holy and is left that way until it dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no פדיון at all, nobody is ever redeeming קדשים to feed to dogs. שמואל still holds that the sanctity truly takes hold of the טריפה's body.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this; the גמרא is changing the wording of a statement
It creates sanctity
To die; it stays holy until it dies

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the animal must be killed. He means the sanctity stays on it, without פדיון, until it dies on its own.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it creates sanctity
(until death,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out all the words in round brackets. Without them, the line reads: it creates sanctity to die.

phrases.english: as he thinks it is permitted to consecrate
blemished animals for the altar;
regarding temurah, it becomes holy;
regarding consecrated offerings, it does not become holy)
to die,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by changing the wording of שמואל's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל allows a טריפה to be redeemed once it has a מום, which would mean redeeming it for dog food.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds a consecrated טריפה is holy until it dies and is never redeemed.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: consecrating a טריפה is like consecrating wood and stones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא disagrees with שמואל. A consecrated טריפה only gets money-sanctity, like wood or stones, so it can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא says: it is nothing more than someone who consecrates plain wood and stones.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is brought that argues with שמואל. רבי אושעיא says the טריפה's body never becomes holy. Only its value is holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person consecrates wood or stones, only their value belongs to הקדש, and they can be redeemed. רבי אושעיא puts a טריפה in that same group. So it has no קדושת הגוף, and redeeming it is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing other than
Wood and stones; things that only have money-sanctity

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear argument. According to שמואל a טריפה gets body-sanctity. According to רבי אושעיא it gets only money-sanctity.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya says:
it is nothing but
like one who consecrates mere wood and stones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that disagrees with שמואל's corrected statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A consecrated טריפה has only money-sanctity, like wood and stones, and may be redeemed.

steps.title: A משנה suggests a טריפה from the start can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that קדשים which became טריפה cannot be redeemed. The wording 'became' suggests that an animal which was a טריפה from the start can be redeemed, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: all קדשים that became טריפה are not redeemed, because we do not redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs. The reason is that they 'became' טריפה. So if they were טריפה from the beginning, they can be redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and draws a careful point from its wording to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only blocks פדיון when the animal became a טריפה after it was consecrated. That suggests an animal that was a טריפה before it was consecrated can be redeemed, like רבי אושעיא says. This goes against שמואל, who says it stays holy until death.

keyTerms.meaning: That became; the change happened after they were consecrated
The reason; used to point out exactly what a rule depends on
From the start
We redeem

phrases.english: We learned in a mishnah:
all consecrated animals that became tereifa,
one may not redeem them,
because one does not redeem consecrated animals
in order to feed them to dogs.
The reason is that they became tereifa,
but if they were tereifa from the start,
one may redeem them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's corrected statement from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a טריפה consecrated from the start stays holy until death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'became' in the משנה suggests that a טריפה from the start can be redeemed.

steps.title: This תנא holds that an animal unfit from the start never gets body-sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this משנה may follow a תנא who holds that an animal not fit to be offered never gets קדושת הגוף. That is why, in his view, it can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this תנא holds: whenever an animal itself is not fit to be offered, קדושת הגוף never takes hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the משנה's point. It is the view of one particular תנא, so it does not have to bind שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's point fits a תנא who says body-sanctity never takes hold of an animal that cannot be offered. That is the same idea as רבי אושעיא. שמואל can therefore follow a different view, and the משנה is not a disproof of him.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
A sage of the משנה period
Not fit in itself to be offered
Sanctity of the body itself, as opposed to holiness of its value alone

steps.whatToRemember: The argument over a טריפה consecrated from the start depends on one question: can קדושת הגוף take hold of an animal that could never be offered? This תנא, like רבי אושעיא, says no.

phrases.english: Perhaps this tanna holds:
anywhere that the animal itself is not fit,
inherent sanctity does not come to rest on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the משנה to one particular תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is a clear disproof of שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects a תנא who holds that no קדושת הגוף takes hold of an unfit animal. שמואל can follow a different view.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's ruling about unusual animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge by quoting רבי אלעזר: animals that are כלאים, יוצא דופן, טריפה, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס are 'not sacred and do not sanctify.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר says that a crossbred animal, an animal born by caesarean section, a טריפה, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not sacred and do not make other animals sacred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against שמואל by first quoting the ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר puts a טריפה on a list of animals that are 'not sacred.' On its own this does not yet attack שמואל. The גמרא first needs to explain what these words mean, which comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species mixed together
An animal born by caesarean section, through the side of the mother
An animal with a fatal defect
An animal whose gender cannot be seen because it is covered
An animal with both male and female features

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Elazar says:
A crossbred animal, an animal born by caesarean section, and a tereifa,
and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite
are not sacred, and they do not make sacred.
phrases.notes: 'Make sacred' means making another animal holy by swapping it in as a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a fresh challenge against שמואל after the answer in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלאים, יוצא דופן, טריפה, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are not sacred and do not make other animals sacred.

steps.title: שמואל explains רבי אלעזר as talking about substitution
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that רבי אלעזר is talking about תמורה: these animals cannot become sacred as a substitute, and they cannot make another animal sacred as their substitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: They do not become sacred through תמורה, and they do not make another animal sacred by making it a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains what רבי אלעזר meant by 'not sacred and do not sanctify.' He says both parts are about the rules of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not sacred' means: if you try to swap one of these animals in for a קרבן, it does not become holy. 'Do not sanctify' means: if one of these animals was consecrated, you cannot swap a regular animal in for it and make that animal holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Swapping a regular animal for a consecrated one, which makes the regular animal holy too
Become sacred
Make something else sacred

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
They are not sacred through substitution,
and they do not make sacred, to create a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of רבי אלעזר's words from step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both halves of רבי אלעזר's ruling are about תמורה: these animals cannot become a substitute, and they cannot create one.

steps.title: רבי מאיר limits the case to an animal that became a טריפה later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר, who asks how an animal that is not sacred could make another animal sacred. He answers that the case must be an animal that was consecrated and only later became a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא that רבי מאיר said: Since they are not sacred, how could they make anything sacred? You only find this in a case where someone consecrated an animal and afterward it became a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר explains which case רבי אלעזר's ruling is talking about. This sets up the inference against שמואל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר sees a problem: if an animal never becomes holy, it is obvious that it cannot pass holiness on to a substitute. So he says that ruling must be about an animal that was consecrated while healthy and then became a טריפה. It became holy at first, so it makes sense to say it still cannot make a substitute.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
From where? How could it be?
You only find this in the case of
It became a טריפה

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Meir said:
But since they are not sacred,
from where would they make sacred?
Rather, you do not find this
except where one consecrates an animal
and afterward it became a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין קְדוֹשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that narrows רבי אלעזר's ruling to one specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling that these animals do not make others sacred applies only to an animal that was consecrated and only afterward became a טריפה.

steps.title: So an animal that was a טריפה from the start gets no inherent holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי מאיר that an animal that was a טריפה from the start never gets קדושת הגוף. This goes against שמואל, who said such an animal becomes holy 'to die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This means that if it was a טריפה from the beginning, קדושת הגוף never rests on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי מאיר's words and uses it to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר limited the case to an animal that became a טריפה after it was consecrated. That implies an animal that was already a טריפה when consecrated never gets body-holiness at all, so it can be redeemed. But שמואל said such an animal is holy until it dies and is never redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows that (the גמרא is drawing an inference)
From the beginning
It does not come down on it; it does not take hold
Holiness of the animal's body itself, as opposed to only holiness of its money value

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, only an animal that became a טריפה after it was consecrated has real body-holiness. One that was a טריפה from the start does not, and that is the problem for שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר never mentions שמואל. The challenge comes from what his words imply about a case he does not discuss directly: an animal that was a טריפה from the start.

phrases.english: This implies that if it was a tereifa from the outset,
inherent sanctity does not rest upon it.
phrases.notes: This clashes with שמואל, who said such an animal is holy 'to die' (step 29).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רבי מאיר's ברייתא in step 35 and turns it against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling (step 29) that a טריפה from the start, once consecrated, is holy 'to die' with קדושת הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר limits the holy case to an animal that became a טריפה later, which implies that a טריפה from the start gets no קדושת הגוף and can be redeemed. That contradicts שמואל.
